from.place: proof: after choosing a global generator, its nonzero restriction to the integral closed fibre makes the zero locus a relative effective Cartier divisor

title: Zero locus of a section over a valuation base is relative Cartier
statement: Let A be a valuation ring, let f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}(A) be proper, flat, and of finite presentation [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], let X_0 be the integral closed fibre [def-pc-integral-scheme], let L be an invertible module on X [def-sc-invertible-module], and let s be a global section of L whose restriction to X_0 is nonzero. Then the zero scheme Z(s) [def-pc-zero-scheme] is a relative effective Cartier divisor on X over \operatorname{Spec}(A) [def-pc-relative-effective-cartier], hence Z(s)\to\operatorname{Spec}(A) is flat.
